newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's BNI down after 1996 result.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's BNI down after 1996 result.

text.p: Disappointment with the 1996 results of PT Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) is behind heavy selling of the stock, analysts and brokers said.
BNI, which recently floated, closed 50 rupiah lower at 1,600 rupiah on Wednesday after earlier falling to 1,575 rupiah in very active trading as 29 million shares changed hands in one day.
On Monday, the day before the state-controlled BNI announced its 1996 net results, it closed at 1,725 rupiah.
BNI announced an unaudited 1996 net profit of 335 billion rupiah, compared with a consensus estimate of 324.6 billion rupiah, but brokers said some investors felt the figure was below expectations.
"Actually the results were in line with market expectations but many investors expected some surprise," Kian Guntur, a broker of Schroeders Indonesia, said.
Another broker with a Japanese firm said the large sell-off was also partly due to a spill-over effect from weak regional market, particularly counters in the finance sector.

"Some investors, particularly local players, expected the result to have been higher on rumours it might receive sudden income from its bad debts which were written-off in previous years," an analyst with Singapore-based brokerage firm said.
He said BNI had indicated during its initial public offering that every year it received back about 25 percent the bad debts it had previously written-off which was treated as income.
This was rumoured to be more than 50 percent in 1996 and this would have boosted earnings to 380 billion rupiah, he added.
"After the 1996 result, we revised up our target BNI's 1997 net in 1997 to 45.2 billion rupiah from 43.0 billion," he said.

He said an expectation of a better net interest margin in 1997 combined with the possibility of a further deposit rate cut due to sustained ample liquidity in the money market convinced him BNI would achieve this target.
A BNI investor relations official said on Wednesday the bank was likely to announce the exact 1997 net profit target at its annual shareholders meeting on April 14.
"We expect a growth of between 27 to 35 percent in the net profit for 1997," the official said.
BNI's total asset at the end of 1996 was 34.8 trillion rupiah, compared with 32.2 trillion rupiah in 1995 with total equity of 2.8 trillion rupiah in 1996 against 1.6 trillion rupiah in 1995.
He said its return on average asset in 1996 was about one percent, against 0.94 percent in 1995, while its return on average equity was 15 percent in 1996 compared with 19.37 percent in 1995.
"The rise in equity which come from the initial public offering last November also helped raise its capital adequacy ratio to 11.7 percent in 1996 from 8.9 percent in 1995," he said.
The bank had raised its net interest margin ratio to 3.02 percent in 1996 from 2.65 percent in June 1996 but it was narrower than the 3.3 percent achieved in 1995, he said.
"Gross loans in 1996 were 23.4 trillion rupiah compared with 19.4 trillion rupiah in 1995," he added.
The bank said total deposits in 1996 were 19.1 trillion rupiah compared with about 17 trillion rupiah in 1995.
"BNI also succeed in keeping its total non-performing loans to total gross loans at about 6.1 percent from 7.2 percent in 1995," the official said.
